The latest scratch run still produced no macOS workflow run: PR #13 was marked ready, retried on the same tree, then closed and its branch deleted. I’m checking the workflow trigger and the current phase record so I can get a real CI verdict if the repo setup allows it, then record the evidence and finish only that phase.

I’m using the repo and bead workflows now: the linked Bob Mac Capture checkout has its own instructions, and the phase close must preserve the exact evidence and leave the epic open. I’m also tracing whether the CI issue is a workflow trigger mismatch or an external GitHub Actions delay.

I found why the earlier snapshots never triggered CI: they were based on a checkout before `master` gained the `ci/**` push trigger and its dedicated scratch verifier. The newer verifier pushes a temporary branch, waits on the exact SHA, prints every macOS step, and removes the branch. I’m fast-forwarding this linked checkout to that CI infrastructure commit while preserving the unrelated dirty scan changes, then I’ll run the verifier against the same source edits.

The fast-forward exposed overlapping upstream formatting edits in four files, so the stash restored the phase changes with conflicts. I’ve kept the stash as a backup and am reconciling those additions onto the new base before running CI; the other edited files and both fixtures are intact.

The checkout is now on `b8ca374` with the dirty-scan edits restored and no unresolved paths; the temporary stash is removed. I’m rerunning the portable build and docs gate on that current tree, then the built-in macOS scratch verifier against its exact snapshot.
